title: promptfoo/promptfoo — Test your prompts, agents, and RAGs. Red teaming/pentesting/vulnerability scanning for AI. Compare performance of GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and more. Simple declarative configs with command line and CI/CD integration. Used by OpenAI and Anthropic.
content:
promptfoo is a CLI and library for evaluating and red-teaming LLM-based apps. Stop using trial-and-error... start shipping secure, reliable agents
Website · Getting Started · Red Teaming · Documentation · Discord
Promptfoo is now part of OpenAI. Promptfoo remains open source and MIT licensed. Read the company update.
npm install -g promptfoo
promptfoo init --example getting-started
Also available via brew install promptfoo and pip install promptfoo. Or use npx promptfoo@latest to run any command without installing.
Most LLM providers require an API key. Set yours as an environment variable:
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-abc123
Run an eval and view results:
cd getting-started
promptfoo eval
promptfoo view
See Getting Started (evals) or Red Teaming (vulnerability scanning) for more!
- Test your prompts and models with automated evaluations
- Secure your LLM apps with red teaming and vulnerability scanning
- Compare models side-by-side (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock, Ollama, and more)
- Automate checks in CI/CD
- Review pull requests for LLM-related security and compliance issues with code scanning
- Share results with your team

report.summary: Promptfoo, now part of OpenAI, is an open-source CLI and library for evaluating, red-teaming, and comparing LLM apps, with CI/CD integration and local privacy.
report.background: LLM app development has moved from simple prompt tweaking to complex agents and RAG systems, making trial-and-error testing risky and expensive. Teams need reproducible ways to compare models, measure quality, and catch security flaws such as prompt injection, jailbreaks, and data leakage before deployment. Promptfoo emerged as a developer-first open-source tool that uses declarative configs to run evals and red-team scans locally, then integrates results into CI/CD pipelines. Its adoption by major AI companies and production apps serving millions of users reflects growing demand for measurable, secure LLM engineering. The announcement that Promptfoo is now part of OpenAI adds a significant vendor-backed chapter while keeping the project MIT licensed and open source.
key_points: Promptfoo lets teams run automated evaluations of prompts, agents, and RAG pipelines. It supports side-by-side model comparisons across OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock, Ollama, and other providers, helping developers choose models based on metrics rather than gut feel.

The platform includes red teaming and vulnerability scanning for LLM applications. It can generate security reports, test for common AI risks, and help teams find weaknesses before attackers or users encounter them in production.

It is designed for developer workflows: a CLI and library with declarative configs, live reload, caching, and CI/CD integration. Teams can automate checks, review pull requests for LLM security and compliance issues, and share results.

Promptfoo says evals run 100% locally, so prompts and sensitive data do not leave the machine. That privacy focus matters for enterprises and regulated industries testing proprietary prompts or customer data.

The project is now part of OpenAI but remains open source and MIT licensed. It is already battle-tested in production apps serving over 10 million users, and installation is available via npm, brew, pip, or npx.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Promptfoo’s move under OpenAI signals that evaluation and security tooling are becoming core infrastructure, not afterthoughts. It may push more vendors to offer rigorous, reproducible testing and red-teaming standards. For developers, the tool lowers the barrier to comparing models, catching regressions, and embedding security checks into CI/CD while keeping sensitive prompts local. For regular users, the broader impact should be more reliable and secure AI applications, with fewer prompt-injection and data-leak failures. However, OpenAI ownership raises legitimate ecosystem-governance questions, so the MIT license and community alternatives will matter for vendor-neutral trust.
report.tools: Try promptfoo via npm, brew, pip, or npx for local evals and red teaming. Also watch DeepEval, Ragas, and TruLens for LLM evaluation; Garak and PyRIT for AI red teaming; and LangSmith for tracing and evaluation workflows. Pair these with GitHub Actions for CI checks and Ollama for local model testing.
